body: - G-Py-7 (wrap external CLIs as typed functions over the injected Runner) is deviated by the changed line in `push_current_branch`:

- This inlines a mutating `git push` argv and checks `result.returncode` ad hoc, when the codebase already ships a typed wrapper that produces the byte-identical argv: `git.push_set_upstream(runner, remote, refspec, *, cwd=None)` in `python/larch/git/git.py`, defined as `_run(runner, ["git", "push", "-u", remote, refspec], cwd=cwd)`. The sibling push path `push_branch` in the same file (`python/larch/git/push.py`) already routes through that wrapper — `git.push_set_upstream(runner, remote, "HEAD", cwd=cwd)` with `remote == "origin"` — so `push_current_branch` is now the lone push site that reaches past the wrapper for the exact argv the wrapper exists to produce. The fix is a drop-in: `result = git.push_set_upstream(runner, "origin", "HEAD", cwd=cwd)`, which converges both push entry points on the typed seam and removes the hardcoded literal. Note the regression test added in `python/tests/git/test_push.py` is unaffected either way, since it only asserts the resolved argv shape.

- Note (no identifier cited, as it is a class-alignment strength rather than a breach): the change does fix the one inconsistent push instance — the in-file sibling `push_branch` was already correct via `push_set_upstream` — so the fix-discipline expectation to converge the class is met on the primary sibling; the only residual is the wrapper-bypass above.
- G-Py-11 is missed by the new line in `python/tests/bgjob/test_wait.py`:

- G-Py-11 requires every lint or type suppression to carry an inline reason on the narrowest scope that works; the canonical forms are `# type: ignore[code]  # reason` (and the pyright analog `# pyright: ignore[code]  # reason`). This suppression is bare: it names the rule (`reportPrivateUsage`) but states no reason, and G-Py-11 explicitly warns that "a bare one reads as unexplained debt." The codebase annotates `reportPrivateUsage` densely — every sibling site in `python/larch/report/final_report.py`, `python/larch/report/run_log_flush.py`, and `python/larch/report/progress_report.py` pairs the pyright ignore with a `# noqa: SLF001 - <reason>` that explains the private access (e.g. "reuse shared outcome display mapping"). A fitting reason here is one clause stating the test monkeypatches a private helper to replay the registry-unlinked-after-result-check race.

- G-Py-11's deviate clause permits a bare suppression only as a ratchet candidate, which requires grandfathering it in `python/suppression-reason-baseline.json` in the same change. G-Py-11 is now mechanically enforced by `python3 python/cli.py lint suppression-reason` (#6750, DONE), and the materialized diff does not update that baseline, so the new suppression is neither reason-annotated nor baselined and would fail `make py-lint-checks-fast`.

- The rest of the diff stays clean against the aspirational guidelines: the bgjob wait fix funnels through the single `_report_missing_registry` reporter so no unfixed same-shape site remains (G-Fix-1/G-Wire-3), reuses the shared `larch.io` read helper (G-IO-1), and ships a regression test that replays the race and asserts DONE with no spurious DEAD (G-Fix-2); the push change routes through the existing typed `git.push_set_upstream` wrapper (G-Py-7) and carries its own argv-asserting test (G-Ext-1); the monkeypatched `race_read_result` callable is a fully typed function, not an untyped lambda (G-Py-14).
